Date: 2027-06-03 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 min | Recording: Fireflies.ai
Agenda: discovery for Dedicated/on-prem option, isolation requirements, burst strategy, compliance needs
Shared materials: 2027-06-03-kestrelin-intake-deck.pdf (uploaded by Alex)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Dr. Lena Cho: Lena here.
[00:08] Marta Lopez: Marta.
[00:09] Ravi Patel: Ravi.
[00:10] Samir Khan: Samir on procurement.
[00:12] Priya Shah: Priya from Redwood.
[00:14] Alex Martinez: Cool. Goal today is to understand your Dedicated vs on‑prem constraints and burst patterns so we can map proposal. I'll hand to Priya for a quick architecture sketch.
[00:25] Priya Shah: Thanks. So Redwood offers Hosted, Dedicated reserve pools, and Private (VPC/on‑prem). For Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools that we manage, with options for isolation—tenant fencing, node‑level reservations, prewarmed hot pools.
[00:40] Dr. Lena Cho: When you say "prewarm hot pools" is that, like, warmed NV cache or actual prestarted containers? We have strict cold‑start issues for inference loads.
[00:48] Priya Shah: It's both. We pre‑provision instances (warm containers) and maintain KV cache warm so the KV/attention cache is hot for common prefixes. There's a tradeoff: more prewarm means higher base cost but lower p99 latency.
[01:02] Ravi Patel: Our use case: batch + real‑time mix. Most requests are ~1.5k input tokens, sometimes 5k for long reports. Typical steady RPS is 25, peeks up to 220 for 7–12 minutes during nightly analysis windows.
[01:20] Alex Martinez: Great, that gives an initial SLO target. Do you have p50/p95 numbers you're targeting?
[01:26] Dr. Lena Cho: p50 under 120ms, p95 under 400ms ideally, but we'll accept p95 up to 600ms during peaks if costs are reasonable.
[01:36] Priya Shah: Understood. For 220 RPS at avg 1.5k tokens we would advise a mixed approach: reserved baseline capacity sized for 40–60 RPS, and a prewarm burst pool for the daily spikes. We can also route lower‑priority requests to cheaper quantized variants.
[01:53] Marta Lopez: About quantization — we have concerns about accuracy drift. How do you guard quality when switching to a quantized variant?
[02:01] Priya Shah: We recommend a shotgun: run canary traffic to the quantized variant, evaluate with your eval set, and Redwood Optimize provides regression alerts tied to prompt sets. But yes, quality monitoring is essential.
[02:14] Dr. Lena Cho: Also, can the Dedicated nodes be isolated for compliance — like physically isolated node pools for PII workloads?
[02:22] Priya Shah: Yes. Dedicated supports tenant‑fenced pools so your jobs only land on nodes reserved to your account. For on‑prem we can do an air‑gapped bundle with a private control plane if needed; that includes KMS/HSM integrations.
[02:36] Ravi Patel: On the HSM topic — we use Thales Luna in our data center. What's the integration surface?
[02:41] Priya Shah: We have an HSM abstraction layer: Redwood's private agent can talk to customer‑managed KMS/HSM via API or PKCS#11 depending on your setup. We'll need network egress rules and certs for the control plane to handshake.
[02:57] Samir Khan: From procurement perspective, what are the licensing term options for Dedicated reserved nodes? Annual only or monthly?
[03:03] Alex Martinez: We offer both monthly and annual reserved commitments. Annual gives better unit economics and burst credits. We'll circulate the pricing sheet.
[03:11] Dr. Lena Cho: Is there an option to burst to public Hosted temporarily if our reserved pool is saturated?
[03:16] Priya Shah: Yes, policy can route to the Hosted catalog under strict rules. For data governance you can opt to disallow Hosted for any PII traffic—those would be blocked and failover to on‑prem or queue.
[03:30] Ravi Patel: How do you handle tenant eviction and noisy neighbor detection? We had problems with ephemeral tenants on other providers where one job took down a whole node.
[03:39] Priya Shah: We use continuous monitoring and preemption policies. For Dedicated we do tenant fencing and cgroup level throttling. For Dedicated pools with strict isolation we can reserve whole nodes per tenant.
[03:50] Marta Lopez: Network topology: If we do on‑prem, does Redwood ship an appliance or do we run a Helm chart?
[03:56] Priya Shah: For on‑prem we offer two modes: a packaged appliance (OVF or container bundle) or a customer‑managed Helm/k8s operator. The appliance is simpler for air‑gapped installs.
[04:08] Dr. Lena Cho: Latency inside DC is critical for us. What about model shard placement across GPUs? We use long‑context models that need multiple GPUs.
[04:16] Priya Shah: The runtime shards KV cache and tensor streams across GPUs and we support model parallel with optimized kernels. For long sequence lengths we choose kernels that minimize inter‑GPU sync. We should run your model artifact to validate.
[04:29] Ravi Patel: Security: audit logs, RBAC, SSO. We need UI and API audit trails retained for 2 years and SAML SSO with SCIM.
[04:38] Alex Martinez: Redwood Console has token‑level cost traces and audit logs; retention is configurable as an add‑on. SAML/SCIM and RBAC are supported for enterprise tiers. We'll attach the compliance pack.
[04:50] Samir Khan: Any surprises on egress costs if we do hybrid?
[04:54] Priya Shah: Hybrid can have egress costs depending on where inference runs and whether logs are sent to Hosted analytics. We can keep telemetry local for on‑prem to avoid egress, though some control plane calls still go to Redwood for management unless you choose fully offline bundle.
[05:09] Dr. Lena Cho: For the PoC we want to validate throughput at our average and peak — can Redwood run an on‑site benchmark, or do you expect us to run it?
[05:17] Priya Shah: We'll do it collaboratively. Priya: we need your model container and a representative traffic file. We'll spin up a dedicated PoC pool—can be on‑prem or in a dedicated cloud region.
[05:28] Priya Shah: Note — if you share model weights, sign the NDA or use containerized artifact with de‑identified data.
[05:34] Ravi Patel: We'll provide a traffic trace and the container image link.
[05:36] Marta Lopez: What about failover SLAs during pre‑warm warmups? If a pool fails during a 10‑minute spike we need fallback to another region.
[05:44] Priya Shah: Redwood provides smart routing policies with region failover and model variant fallback. For hard failure we recommend multi‑region Dedicated or a hybrid fallback to Hosted if compliance allows.
[05:55] Alex Martinez: Quick note on economics—prewarming to cover 220 RPS 24/7 is expensive. We typically size reserved baseline for steady and prewarm targeted hotpool for the 7–12 minute spikes. There are also options for burst credits/auto‑scale buffers.
[06:10] Dr. Lena Cho: OK. Procurement wants a cost estimate for two options: (A) Dedicated in Redwood cloud with tenant fencing, (B) On‑prem private bundle with HSM integration.
[06:20] Alex Martinez: We'll produce both. Alex to include CAPEX vs OPEX notes for on‑prem.
[06:25] Samir Khan: Timeline — if we sign, how long to provision a Dedicated baseline?
[06:29] Priya Shah: Dedicated baseline typically 2–4 weeks depending on node type and quotas; on‑prem bundle is 4–8 weeks for air‑gapped integration and HSM cert exchange.
[06:40] Ravi Patel: Any gotchas with model size? We use a 80B parameter model with 64k context.
[06:47] Priya Shah: 80B + 64k is heavy. We need to validate memory footprint, possible quantization, and model parallel config. We'll ask for a trimmed container or run a memory‑profiling pass in the PoC.
[06:59] Dr. Lena Cho: Can we keep debug logs locally? We don't want prompt data in Hosted logs.
[07:04] Priya Shah: Yes, logs can be configured to never leave your VPC; control plane telemetry can be minimized or delivered via secure agent.
[07:11] Alex Martinez: Last section — decision criteria? What's most important?
[07:15] Marta Lopez: Security >Latency >Cost in that order.
[07:19] Dr. Lena Cho: Also reliability during scheduled nightly spikes.
[07:22] Samir Khan: Procurement needs a simple TCO table to compare Dedicated vs on‑prem vs hosted.
[07:27] Alex Martinez: Understood. We'll send a pricing + TCO template.
[07:31] Priya Shah: I'll own the perf baseline and the PoC plan.
[07:35] Alex Martinez: Great. Any final questions?
[07:37] Ravi Patel: One — do you have examples of other pharma/therapeutics customers doing on‑prem with HSM?
[07:42] Priya Shah: Yes, we have references; will include anonymized case studies in the security pack.
[07:49] Alex Martinez: Thanks all. Recap in the notes and action items — we'll aim to follow up by next Tuesday with pricing and the perf run plan.
[07:58] Dr. Lena Cho: Thanks.
[08:00] Meeting end.
notes_summary: Customer (Kestrelin) is evaluating Dedicated vs on‑prem for compliance and bursty nightly workloads. Key constraints: HSM (Thales Luna), long‑context 80B model, peaks up to 220 RPS for 7–12 minutes, strict audit log retention, and preference for tenant‑fenced dedicated nodes. Redwood proposed a hybrid: reserved baseline + prewarm hotpool + quantized fallback. Next steps include pricing, SOC2/on‑prem docs, and a perf PoC with customer model container.
questions: Can Redwood route burst traffic to Hosted while ensuring PII doesn't leave customer's boundary?
What is the integration pattern for Thales Luna HSM?
How long to provision on‑prem vs dedicated in cloud?
